response.summary: The Home surface rules in style.css lines 477–548 are added after the baseline stylesheet's last line (476). Every new component rule is scoped to main[data-route="home"]. The only exceptions are the route-guarded html/body ground selectors, so shared .card/.panel/.session rules for subpages stay untouched. Most of the plan matches the code: rail separators for all five width ranges, ledger sheet and row geometry, calendar inline alignment (21/25/19/17px), strip-only day edges via media plus a nested container query, the --muted override on the rail, and the ledger numeral colour. My hand calculations put contrast at about 4.7–5.0:1 for the measured text-on-surface pairs. One material problem remains: the resume (dark workspace) changes go beyond the plan's 'reduce only its ambient shadow' limit. There are also two lower-severity points.

findings.evidence: The plan says 'Preserve the16px resume radius and inset highlight while reducing only its ambient shadow' and 'Do not flatten the intended focal point'. Line 483 swaps the 0 0 0 1px rgb(19 23 24/.9) ring for a real 1px #303834 border. That adds 2px to the box and lightens the outer edge. Line 484 also cuts .resume-copy padding from 26px 30px 24px to 24px 26px. Lines 536 and 541 change the ≤640 and ≤380 padding too (24/20/22 becomes 22/20, and 22/16/20 becomes 22/16), which shifts the statement, track and Continue positions on mobile. None of these changes is in the plan.
findings.fix: Restore the base padding by deleting the Home .resume-copy rules on lines 484, 536 and 541. Keep the original 0 0 0 1px rgb(19 23 24 / .9) ring in place of border:1px solid #303834, so the only change is the ambient shadow: main[data-route="home"] .resume{box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .12) inset,0 0 0 1px rgb(19 23 24 / .9),0 8px 18px -12px rgb(19 23 24 / .5)}. If the border or padding change is wanted, record it in the plan or review log first.

findings.evidence: Plan item 7 asks for a 'raised finder'. Line 514 instead takes the finder from #fff with var(--lift) (inset highlight, 1px ring, 12px/28px drop) down to #fdfcf8 with a single 0 1px 2px shadow. On the new #e6e7e2 ground it ends up less raised than before; only hover goes back to #fff.
findings.fix: Keep the finder's resting background #fff, or keep a short two-part lift such as 0 0 0 1px ring plus a 0 2px 4px drop. Otherwise, record that flattening the finder was intended and check it against the 1366px before render.

findings.evidence: Above 1279px, .desk keeps align-items:stretch (line 132), so the .desk-side rail box still grows to the resume's height. align-content:start on line 485 only top-packs the grid rows inside it. The rail has a #e0e2db background, so if the resume is taller than coach + session (for example with no saved note, or at 1440 where the h2 clamp grows), an empty mid-tone band shows at the bottom of the rail. That is exactly the 'manufactured empty space' the plan wanted to avoid. Line 485 also sets grid-template-rows:auto auto at every width, which overrides the base grid-template-rows:none at ≤1279 (line 386). The result is an empty implicit row; with gap:0 it is harmless.
findings.fix: At 1366 and 1440, check the rail bottom in both the empty-note and saved-note states. If a band appears, add main[data-route="home"] .desk-side{align-self:start} above 1279, or accept the band and record that choice. You can also limit grid-template-rows:auto auto to a min-width:1280px query.

coverage: Read the full runtime style.css (548 lines), including every appended Home-scoped rule on lines 477–548
Read the end of the saved baseline reviews/home-surfaces-before-20261026/style.css and confirmed it ends at line 476 with no data-route rules, so the change is the appended block

Read the Home markup generators in app.js (assignmentRows, coachCard, sessionCard, home, daysHTML, agendaHTML) to confirm class names, element types (article rows, so :first-of-type and :last-child match), and that .ledger, .week, .coach and .session are .card elements
Checked specificity of the Home rules against the base media and container rules (row ::before offsets at ≤640/≤380, .card padding at ≤640/≤380, .week ordering at ≤1279/≤640/≤380)
Traced the rail separator axis for each width range against the base .desk-side column counts (>1279, 1000–1279, 721–999, 641–720, ≤640)
Checked the calendar inline-alignment arithmetic against ledger padding plus border at each width
Checked that the day-border logic targets the seven-column strip only (media plus a nested @container(width>36rem) on the .week container) and leaves the selected day's border alone
Calculated WCAG contrast by hand: --muted #616660 on #eceee7 is about 5.0:1, rail #596058 on #e0e2db about 4.96:1, and --muted on the #e6e7e2 ground about 4.71:1
limitations: I could not run node --check, the Playwright/Edge scripts (capture-11, calendar-internal, interactions, surfaces.cjs), or any rendering. Rendered ground L* separation, layout overflow, 200% text behaviour, the 1920px gutters and subpage computed-style equality are all unverified.

I could not hash files. The manifest SHA256 values, the baseline hash fb067868…, and whether lines 1–476 are byte-identical to the baseline are not independently confirmed; I only compared the tail of the baseline by eye.
The tracked diff given to me was empty (diff_sha256 is the empty-string hash), so this review is based on reading the runtime file directly against the saved baseline.
Files outside the inspection scope were read only for context and are not approved: app.js, index.html, the review archives, evidence artifacts and verification scripts.
I did not inspect the user screenshot or the before/after renders, so I make no visual-quality or taste judgement.
